title: Looking into the Black Box: Monitoring Computer Architecture Simulations in Real-Time with AkitaRTM
problem: Computer architecture simulators operate as black boxes with minimal transparency during execution, preventing users from identifying issues in real-time and causing wasted computational resources and human debugging effort.
motivation: Computer architects need real-time visibility and interactive control over simulations to efficiently validate novel chip designs and debug problems.
method: AkitaRTM is an interactive web-based tool designed after studying what slows down computer architects in their work. It shows you what's happening in a simulator in real time and lets you control how it runs through a simple, easy-to-use interface. The tool was tested with two case studies (one actually found a simulator bug that got fixed) and a user study where computer architects confirmed it was helpful.
key_novelty: An interactive web-based tool that lets you watch and control computer architecture simulations in real time, revealing hidden execution so you can debug.
contributions: AkitaRTM tool enabling real-time monitoring and interactive control of computer architecture simulations
Design methodology grounded in computer architects' actual workflow inefficiencies
Practical validation through case studies demonstrating bug identification and simulator patch generation
User study showing improvements in visibility, debugging capability, and educational understanding of simulators

metrics.other: case study utility, user study satisfaction and learning outcomes

primary_theme: Real-time simulation monitoring and debugging tool
